title: Ketoanalogue Supplementation for Muscle Protection in chronic kidney disease (stade 4 and 5) Patients with Moderately Low Protein Diet
official: Ketoanalogue Supplementation for Muscle Protection in CKD 4 and 5 Patients with Moderately Low Protein Diet
summary: Main objective: To determine the effect of Ketoanalogue supplementation on sarcopenia at 12 months in patients with stage 4 or 5 CKD and dietary protein intake between 0.6 and 0.8 g/kg/d
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men or women older than 18 years
2. Stage 4 or 5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (eGFR with CKD-EPI 2009 creatinine equation < 30 mL/min/m2)
3. Protein intake 0.6-0.8 g/kg/d (estimated with dietary survey)
4. patient with social security cover
5. Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hospitalization in the past 3 months
2. Patient under a legal protection (curatorship or tutorship)
3. Corticosteroids (> 7.5 mg/d), cytotoxic or immunosuppressive drugs
4. Severe symptomatic heart (NYHA 3 or 4) or liver failure (Child Pugh B or C)
5. Respiratory failure requiring oxygenotherapy
6. Ongoing infection, autoimmune disease or cancer
7. Pregnant (e.g., positive human chorionic gonadotrophin [HCG] test) or lactating patients
8. Patients with psychiatric or cognitive disorders rendering them unable to give written informed consent
9. Hypersensitivity to the active substances in Ketosteril
10. Hypercalcaemia
